issue.title: Retire ace_refresh_tokens
issue.description: Gate ACE and proc refreshes on per-surface stat-only change tokens.

task_type_fields.remove_when: A soak on both Linux and macOS meets the idle CPU and freshness targets, with token-gated refreshes remaining correct under watcher and watcherless operation.
task_type_fields.when_disabled: ACE auto-refresh keeps today's watcher-aware path, including the watcherless unconditional full reconcile, and ProcObserver parses the durable proc store on every poll.
task_type_fields.when_enabled: ACE auto-refresh and ProcObserver gate expensive surface loads on per-surface stat-only change tokens, while watcher dirty flags, exact agent deltas, and the sanity interval still force a refresh.

payload.entry: From the sase-wn land agent: phase sase-wn.5 recorded a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP to capture the 30-minute watcherless ACE idle CPU soak on Linux and macOS (idle CPU, stall-watchdog records, RSS trajectory); no soak was captured during the epic. That soak is exactly this flag's remove-when condition, so the proposal is routed here rather than to a new task. Capture recipe: docs/perf_runbook.md 'Idle-host CPU diet' (steps 3-5).

Epic sase-1jc authorizes retiring ace_refresh_tokens, superseding the soak wait. Removed the registry definition and Off branches in proc_observer._store_rows and event_refresh auto-refresh; stat-only token gating with dirty/sanity recovery is now unconditional. Verified: test_proc_observer_tokens, auto-refresh debounce + notifications suites green.
